## The question

Using IPEDS data on credit hours and completions, this project measures how much of their own curriculum universities outsource to AP and transfer credit, and whether individual universities and state systems are becoming more efficient at producing degrees over time.

## Interactive tools

### Illustration: where a degree's credits come from

This simple calculator shows the accounting idea behind the measure. It is illustrative arithmetic, not results from the data.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof required = Inputs.range([60, 150], {step: 1, value: 120, label: "Credits required for degree"})
viewof outside = Inputs.range([0, 60], {step: 1, value: 15, label: "% from AP / dual / transfer"})
viewof excess = Inputs.range([0, 40], {step: 1, value: 10, label: "Excess credits taken (%)"})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
earned = required * (1 + excess / 100)
outsideCr = required * outside / 100
inhouse = earned - outsideCr
md`A graduate earns about **${earned.toFixed(0)}** credits. **${outsideCr.toFixed(0)}** arrive from outside, so the university delivers **${inhouse.toFixed(0)}** itself, or **${(100 * inhouse / earned).toFixed(0)}%** of the total.`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  height: 110,
  x: {label: "Credits", domain: [0, 210]},
  y: {axis: null},
  color: {legend: true, domain: ["Delivered by university", "From outside"], range: ["#1f4e79", "#9cb9d6"]},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX([
      {src: "Delivered by university", v: inhouse},
      {src: "From outside", v: outsideCr}
    ], Plot.stackX({x: "v", fill: "src"})),
    Plot.ruleX([required], {stroke: "#c0392b", strokeDasharray: "4,3"}),
    Plot.text([required], {x: d => d, text: () => "Required", dy: -40, fill: "#c0392b"})
  ]
})
```
